title: Protocol to perform dynamic microfluidic single-cell cultivation of C. glutamicum
protocol: Inoculate 10 mL CGXII-medium in a 100-mL baffled shaking flask from a glycerol stock aliquot.
Incubate overnight at 30°C on a shaker at 120 rpm.
From the preculture, inoculate the main culture at an OD600 of 0.05–0.1.
Incubate the main culture on a shaker at 30°C for 3–4 h until the OD600 increases by at least 1.5-fold.
Turn on the temperature control of the microscope cage.
Let objects inside the cage warm up to prevent material expansion due to temperature changes.
Prepare the flow periphery.
Prepare the medium.
Prepare and mount the microfluidic chip.
Connect the periphery as shown in Figure 7A.
Place a tissue beneath the needles to absorb any potential leakage.
Ensure that the needles and tubing do not obscure the imaging region.
Optimize positioning so one single bacterial cell is caught in the center of the chamber after loading.
Apply a drop of immersion oil on the 100× oil objective as shown in Figure 7B.
Place the chip mounted on a holder on the microscope’s stage.
Fixate the holder to prevent shifting during live-cell imaging.
Tape the microfluidic chip to the holder from below, ensuring no tape covers the cut-out window.
Load cells into the microfluidic chambers.
Fill a 1-mL syringe with bacteria suspension from the main culture.
Dilute bacteria suspension if OD600 exceeds 0.3–0.4 using medium.
Connect the syringe to the loading tubing and fill the tube with suspension.
Insert the needle connected to the syringe with the suspension into the outlet of the microfluidic structure.
Flush the structure very gently with suspension.
Remove emerging droplets from the inlets with a tissue.
Check at least 10 chambers across the control and switching zones for an adequate number (1–4) of cells.
Do not remove the drops formed on the inlets after loading.
If the number of chambers with loaded cells is too low, flush a little more forcefully in a pulsating manner to raise the flexible PDMS slightly.

If the loading is still insufficient, insert an air bubble into the channels and move them back and forth along the chamber arrays via the outlet by reversing the flow or via the inlet by re-inserting the needle without a drop on the needle’s tip.
Optional: Remove any cells present in the channels and inlets by flushing the chip with a syringe of medium.
Insert the medium-needle into the outlet to decrease the risk of inlets overgrowing with bacteria during cultivation.
Start the pumps with a pressure of 15–20 mbar.
When the first drop of medium forms at the needle tip, insert the needles into the inlets.
Increase the pressure of the pumps to the level that has been chosen as pressure pair of flow profile P1 in step 14.
Attach the outlet tubing when the first drop forms on the outlet.
Fixate the tube’s end to the waste container using tape.
Make sure that all tubing is not under tension.
Center and focus the light path using Köhler illumination.
Adjust the phase ring according to the manufacturer’s manual.
Set the phase contrast channel with a light intensity of 10%.
Set the exposure time of 100 ms for acquisition.
Adjust the frequency of acquisition to 10 min.
Search for chambers with one to four cells in both control regions and the switching zone.
Save the positions for time-lapse imaging.
Start the acquisition and the pump program simultaneously.
Check the running experiment for focus loss after 1 hour.
Readjust the focus if necessary.
End the acquisition after the planned experiment duration.
Tidy up.
Stop the image acquisition.
Stop the pump program.
Turn off the pumps after finishing the experiment.
Exchange one medium reservoir with an ink reservoir.
Turn the pumps on and set the pressures according to flow profile P1 and P2.
Observe critical regions for correct spatial flow profile.
Discard the chip and tubing used in the experiment.
Detach needles from tubing and collect them in isopropanol.
Place the collected needles in ultrasonic bath for 90 minutes.
Discard isopropanol and rinse needles with ddH2O water.
Remove any loose syringe adapters dissolved by isopropanol.
Place rinsed needles in water in an ultrasonic bath for 90 minutes.
Discard water and repeat step of placing needles in ultrasonic bath.
Autoclave the needles in a glass petri dish for sterilization.
Remove oil film from objective’s lens with a soft tissue.
Wipe the objective with an isopropanol-soaked tissue afterwards.
Clean pressure caps and tubing adaptors by washing them with dH2O.
Discard data not fit or necessary for the analysis during the cropping process in the microscope software.
Note: If cells are washed out of the chamber, discard the data for that position.
Crop edges of the acquired picture if recording the whole field of view to focus only on the chamber.
Save image sequences in a usable file format such as OME-TIFF or Nikon-specific nd2 stacks.
Use command “split multipoint” to save Nikon-specific nd2 stacks.
Pre-process images using Fiji and a self-tailored macro for automated cell detection optimization.
Choose a region on the PDMS as reference for stabilizing the image data.
Stabilize the movement of the images in a stack using the "Image Stabilizer" plugin.
Select a reference area on the PDMS structures for stabilization.
Rotate the chamber to ensure it is straight.
Crop the image stack to remove refraction from the chamber edges.
Save the cropped image stack as a TIFF file.
Discard data not fit or necessary for analysis during cropping.
Load the image stack from step 37 into FIJI.
Open the macro “colony segmentation” by dragging the file into FIJI.
Set initial image analysis parameters in FIJI.
Draw a region of interest around the colony or choose to analyze the whole chamber.
Press "Run" in the macro editor.
Set boundaries for circularity and area for cell detection.
Tick "Average values per frame" and "Single-cell values".
Increase the number of clusters if difficulties arise with cell detection.
Select measurements such as mean gray values for fluorescence data analysis.
Create a binary mask for cell detection.
Set a threshold after clustering is performed.
Press “ok” to continue once the threshold result looks correct.
Check if the box “black background” is ticked under Process > Binary > Options if the macro segments the background instead of cells.
Set an adjustable watershed value for splitting wrongly connected cells during clustering.
Use the preview to determine the appropriate watershed value before continuing.
Detect the cells with “Analyze Particles.”
Count any uncounted cells by hand using the multipoint tool or re-run the macro with different settings.
Save the results table for further analysis.
